facts.fact: The pepper hunters' shelter above the tree line is a stacked-stone hut with a turf roof, one low door and a hearth, used in the dry months by wild-pepper cutters; Kesu's grandson drew the route on a tally stick.
facts.why: needed because the beat sends them to a pepper hunters' shelter above the tree line.

facts.fact: Thilak's inventory: forty-one season flasks (forty plus a spare Pavi carried), nine hooked tapping knives, and a small copy of Pachan's grove map showing the north slope and three trees that run best at noon. Neela refuses the spare flask.
facts.why: beat names the flasks, tapping knives and grove map; the spare and Neela's refusal keep her ache plausible.

facts.fact: The sealed last quire holds one sheet headed 'Sold to the crown' listing thirty ledger numbers with years and sums in panam, each with a folded-wing sunbird in the margin, and behind it the cut stubs of thirty leaves.

Vellan holds his own page (read to him by Neela earlier) and walks up unscented by resin; he says the queen's night-guard numbers thirty-one, that four escort guards crossed the shut pass by the goat path (he taught two of them), and that the queen witnessed each guard's first turning. He does not name any night-shape aloud.
facts.why: beat requires Vellan to confirm the queen's guard are odiyans and the escort among them.

facts.fact: Vellan gives Kamalakshi a carved wooden bird; she keeps it but says she has not forgiven him. Devan leaves a folded cloth beside him.
facts.why: ties Vellan's established bird-carving habit to the scene.
